Hi Alex — great to connect. Quick timezone check so we avoid back-and-forth: when you say "Thursday 10:00" / "Friday 14:00", is that BST (British Summer Time / UTC+1) or another local time?

To make scheduling easier, here are the equivalent options in common zones we usually confirm with customers (including our US teams):

- Thursday 10:00 BST = Thursday 09:00 GMT / Thursday 04:00 PT / Thursday 07:00 ET / Thursday 11:00 CET
- Friday 14:00 BST = Friday 13:00 GMT / Friday 06:00 PT / Friday 09:00 ET / Friday 15:00 CET

If you are indeed on BST (UTC+1) then the Thursday 10:00 BST option would be:
- 10:00 BST / 05:00 PT / 08:00 ET / 11:00 CET / 04:30 IST (for colleagues in India)

We have the full demo team available on Thursday 10:00 BST (which is Thursday 02:00 PT / 05:00 ET for some of our east-coast folks); if that time is too early for your side we can move to Friday 14:00 BST.

If either works, I can send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (10–15 min intro + 30 min live demo + Q&A). Also attaching a one-page agenda for visibility.

Note: US daylight saving is in effect — PT/ET times above account for DST. Happy to confirm in UTC if that helps remove any ambiguity.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
